title: Batang 90s: Why Filipinos Miss the 1990s So Much, Explained | Papel Tales
description:
Why are Filipinos so obsessed with being a "Batang 90s"? From patintero and tumbang preso on the street, teks, jolens and trumpo in every pocket, and candlelit brownout nights, to after-school Sineskwela and the texting boom, this paper-cut story explains what growing up in the 1990s Philippines was like, and what science says about why nostalgia feels so good.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Prologue
0:28 What is a Batang 90s?
0:50 The street was the playground
1:19 Pocket treasures
1:47 Brownout nights
2:12 After-school TV
2:35 The texting generation
2:56 Why we feel nostalgia
3:32 Why it still matters
3:54 Epilogue

SOURCES
- Republic Act No. 7648, Electric Power Crisis Act of 1993 (5 April 1993)
- Edgardo J. Angara, "Emergency powers and other options", BusinessMirror (2014): brownouts averaging 8 to 10 hours a day
- Sine'skwela (ABS-CBN, from 6 June 1994) and Hiraya Manawari (from 7 October 1995), Knowledge Channel / ABS-CBN News
- "The Philippine text messaging phenomenon", Philippine Star, 15 May 2001
- Wildschut, Sedikides, Arndt and Routledge, "Nostalgia: Content, triggers, functions", Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 91(5), 975-993 (2006)
- Rubin, Wetzler and Nebes (1986), autobiographical memory across the lifespan (the reminiscence bump)
